faqs.q: What is the formula to convert hourly to annual pay in Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: Is salary sacrifice a fringe benefit?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, so the basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

If you work 38 hours each week, your annual gross is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 (38 × 52). For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,261.44. If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is your weekly pay multiplied by 2 (e.g., $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80).

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for estimating your annual earnings.

## Different Pay Rates: Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

Australia has several pay standards:

- **National Minimum Wage**: From 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission sets this at $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week ($1,004.90 per week).
- **Award rates**: Many industries have modern awards that set higher minimum pay rates for specific roles. These are determined by the Fair Work Ombudsman and may include penalty rates for weekends or overtime.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Our [timesheet](/) lets you check a box to add this loading automatically.

Remember that the Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings, such as full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). These are averages across all industries and states, not a median for your specific job. Your actual rate may differ based on your award, enterprise agreement, or individual contract.

## Tax, Medicare, and Superannuation

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here).

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay by your employer, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 in super (12% of $60,000). This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

## Salary Sacrifice as a Fringe Benefit

A common question is: **is salary sacrifice a fringe benefit?** Yes, salary sacrifice arrangements—where you forgo part of your salary in exchange for benefits like a car, laptop, or additional super contributions—are considered fringe benefits under the Fringe Benefits Tax (FBT) legislation. Your employer may pay FBT on the value of the benefit, and your taxable income is reduced by the sacrificed amount. However, our calculator does not account for salary sacrifice, so your actual take-home pay and tax position may differ. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet and Other Resources

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page where you can enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual, check the box to add 25% loading—do not type a rate that already includes casual loading. The tool then estimates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, tax, Medicare, and super.

## Important Notes and Limitations

This estimate assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold, and Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for award rates and the Australian Taxation Office for your personal tax situation.
